title: Meme Runway Studio
premise: A short fashion-themed casual game where the player traces outfit templates in two runway design rounds and then completes a three-question style trivia segment.
interaction_model: Touch/pointer-based canvas drawing plus button-driven UI choices for progression and quiz answers.
objective: Finish two guided fashion sketch rounds and answer the fashion quiz with the highest possible score.
progression: Round 1 tracing, Round 2 tracing, then a 3-question multiple-choice quiz followed by a score screen and restart option.
theme: Fashion runway, meme-inspired styling, colorful pop design, and light trivia.
likely_audience: Casual mobile players, kids, and players who enjoy fashion-themed mini-games with simple interactions.
confidence_notes: High confidence on the state flow, controls, and quiz structure because they are explicit in code. Moderate confidence on genre labeling because the game mixes guided drawing, dress-up framing, and quiz gameplay without scoring the drawing quality itself.
recreation_prompt: Create a short mobile-friendly browser game called "Meme Runway Studio" with a flashy neon-memphis fashion-show presentation. The game should open on a full-screen canvas where the player traces a dashed outfit guide using touch or mouse input, choosing from a small palette of bright colors and using Clear and Done buttons. Structure the experience into two guided design rounds: first a meme-themed outfit silhouette, then a viral dress silhouette. After the player taps Done on each round, show a Next button to continue. Once both drawing rounds are complete, switch into a fashion trivia phase with a centered overlay card asking three multiple-choice questions about clothing and color basics, advancing immediately after each answer and tracking score. Use upbeat background music that changes between the design phase and quiz phase, plus short click, success, fail, and win sounds. Show a small reaction image or animated feedback card for correct and incorrect actions, and present a final score screen with a playful title and a restart button labeled like a remix or replay. Keep the game lightweight, highly readable on phones, visually bold, and focused on a simple loop of trace, progress, answer trivia, and replay rather than deep simulation or precise scoring of the drawing.
